title: Times Tables to 5
subtitle: Factors 0 to 5
bounds: Factors 0 to 5. Forms: R a × b = ?, C a × ? = p, S ? × b = p (a missing factor is never 0). T1 R: a fact with a 0, 1, 2 or 5 (32 prompts); T2 R: both factors 1-5 (25); T3 R: both 2-5 (at least 12 items) and C with 2 or 5 as the first factor, factors 1-5 (at least 8; 26 prompts in all); T4 C: factors 1-5 (25); T5 S: both 2-5 (at least 12 items) and C: both 2-5 (32 prompts in all). At most 6 prompts per tier with a 0 factor. Wrong choices are distinct non-negative whole numbers up to 999. R: at least two within the larger factor of the answer (at least 2), at most one far. C and S: at least two within 2 of the answer, at most one far. Answer ranks (smallest to largest of the four) each hold 15 to 35 percent of a tier.

tiers.name: Times 0, 1, 2, 5
tiers.description: Facts with 0, 1, 2 or 5. Zero groups make nothing; double for 2s.

tiers.name: All to 5 × 5
tiers.description: Every fact with factors 1 to 5. Use doubles and count by 5s.

tiers.name: Times 2 to 5
tiers.description: Facts with factors 2 to 5, plus a missing factor in the 2s and 5s.

tiers.name: Missing factors
tiers.description: Missing factor: 3 × ? = 12. Ask what times 3 makes 12.

tiers.name: Missing first factors
tiers.description: First factor missing: ? × 4 = 12, or a missing second factor. Factors 2 to 5.

GROUP_OFF.student: One group too many or too few. Count the groups, then the size of each.
GROUP_OFF.teacher: Off by one group: a × (b + 1), a × (b − 1), (a + 1) × b or (a − 1) × b.

ADDED.student: × means equal groups, not +. 4 × 3 is 4 groups of 3, which is 12.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the factors instead of multiplying: 4 × 3 = 7.

MISSING_ONE_OFF.student: Check it: multiply your number by the shown one. Does it make the total?
MISSING_ONE_OFF.teacher: Missing factor one too high or too low: counted the groups wrong, or never multiplied back to check.

MISSING_SUBTRACTED.student: Not subtraction. Ask: this number times what makes the total?
MISSING_SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts the shown factor from the product (p − k) instead of dividing the product by it.

MISSING_PRODUCT.student: The total is the product, not the missing factor. Multiply back to check.
MISSING_PRODUCT.teacher: Writes the product as the missing factor: the number already given in the equation.
